questions.question: What is the distinguishing advantage of a PPT algorithm D between distributions D0 and D1?
questions.explanation: Advantage measures the gap between the probability D outputs 1 under each distribution. It ranges from 0 (no ability to distinguish) to 1 (perfect distinguishing).

questions.question: Which of the following functions is negligible in n?
questions.explanation: 2^{-n} shrinks faster than any inverse polynomial — for any polynomial p, eventually 2^{-n} < 1/p(n). The others are non-negligible: 1/n is 1/poly, 1/√n is superpolynomial but still non-negligible, and 0.001 is a constant.

questions.question: If SD(D0, D1) = 0.4, what is the maximum possible advantage of any distinguisher (PPT or unbounded)?
options: 0.4 — SD upper-bounds every distinguisher's advantage
0.2 — you divide SD by 2 for the advantage
0.8 — you double SD for the game-form advantage
It depends on the specific distinguisher
questions.explanation: SD(D0, D1) equals the advantage of the optimal unbounded distinguisher and upper-bounds all others. No distinguisher, PPT or unbounded, can exceed SD.

questions.question: A PRG stretches 128-bit seeds to 256-bit outputs. Why is this computationally indistinguishable from uniform despite having large statistical distance from uniform?
options: The image of G has size 2^128 out of 2^256 strings; enumerating it takes 2^128 time, which is not PPT
The PRG output always has min-entropy 256 bits
The PRG is a bijection so its output is uniform over its range
Statistical distance and computational indistinguishability are the same thing
questions.explanation: The unbounded distinguisher D(x)='is x in image(G)?' wins with Adv≈1 — so SD≈1. But finding the image requires enumerating 2^128 seeds, which is not polynomial time. A PPT adversary cannot perform this check.

questions.question: How does the hybrid argument use computational indistinguishability?
options: Build a chain D0, D1, …, Dk of distributions; sum negligible per-hop advantages to bound Adv(D0, Dk)
Show SD(D0, Dk) = 0 by induction
Replace each distribution with its min-entropy equivalent
Apply the leftover hash lemma at each hop
questions.explanation: By the triangle inequality for advantage, Adv(D0, Dk) ≤ Σ Adv(D_{i}, D_{i+1}). Each hop is negligible by assumption; a polynomial sum of negligible functions is still negligible.

questions.question: What does it mean for two distributions to be computationally indistinguishable (D0 ≈_c D1)?
options: For every PPT distinguisher D, Adv_D(n) is negligible in the security parameter n
No distinguisher of any kind can tell them apart
The min-entropy of D0 equals the min-entropy of D1
questions.explanation: Computational indistinguishability restricts to PPT adversaries. It does not require SD to be small — a PRG's output can be statistically far from uniform yet computationally indistinguishable from it.

questions.question: Which containment is correct?
options: Perfectly secure ⊆ statistically secure ⊆ computationally secure
Computationally secure ⊆ statistically secure ⊆ perfectly secure
Statistically secure ⊆ computationally secure ⊆ perfectly secure
The three notions are incomparable
questions.explanation: Perfect security (SD=0) implies statistical security (SD≤negl), which implies computational security (no PPT has non-negligible advantage). The converses all fail.

questions.question: In the IND game, the challenger picks b ← {0,1} and sends x ← D_b to the distinguisher D, who outputs b'. What is the advantage formula?
options: Pr[b' = b]
questions.explanation: A random guesser wins with probability 1/2. Advantage = how much better than random = |Pr[win] - 1/2| × 2, normalised to [0,1]. Equivalent to |Pr[D=1|D0] - Pr[D=1|D1]|.
